findings.title: proxy --help omits restart and Reconnect steps
findings.problem: AC9 requires `codemie proxy --help`, docs/COMMANDS.md and README.md to list reset-mcp-auth with the restart and Reconnect steps. README.md and COMMANDS.md carry them, but `proxy --help` shows only the one-line description (index.ts:439); the steps are attached solely to `reset-mcp-auth --help` through addHelpText (index.ts:441). The code comment at index.ts:436 states this.
findings.impact: Partial on a required story criterion, so graded critical: a user reading `codemie proxy --help` sees the command without the Reconnect and re-run steps. Reachability confirmed by reading the registration; the consequence is limited to help-text discoverability.
findings.recommendation: Show RESET_NEXT_STEPS next to reset-mcp-auth in `codemie proxy --help` (for example `proxy.addHelpText('after', ...)` on the parent command) and keep the subcommand help as it is.
findings.check_notes: index.ts:124 chains .addHelpText('after', ...RESET_NEXT_STEPS) onto the parent proxy command, so `proxy --help` ends with the restart, Reconnect and re-run lines; the subcommand help at index.ts:442 is kept

fix.change: proxy command now appends the restart and Reconnect steps (RESET_NEXT_STEPS) to `proxy --help` via addHelpText('after')
fix.test: n/a (tests only on request per AGENTS.md); scratchpad probe asserts proxy --help carries RESET_NEXT_STEPS, RED before, GREEN after

findings.title: Duplicate error-code helper in two modules
findings.problem: `errorCode` (desktop-mcp-auth.ts:29-32) and `errorCodeOf` (reset-mcp-auth-orchestrator.ts:52-55) are the same function written twice.
findings.impact: No behavior consequence today; the copies can drift apart. Trigger: a later edit to only one of them. Reachability confirmed by reading both modules.
findings.recommendation: Export one helper (from desktop-mcp-auth.ts or a shared util) and import it in the orchestrator.

findings.title: Read-modify-write can overwrite a concurrent Desktop write
findings.problem: clearDesktopMcpSignIns reads config.json (line 56), then writes the parsed object minus one key (line 72) with no re-check in between. If Claude Desktop writes the file in that window, its newer settings are replaced by the stale copy, contradicting the docs' claim that every other setting is left as it was. Read of the function confirms there is no lock or mtime check.
findings.impact: Narrow trigger: a Desktop write inside the milliseconds between read and rename, with Desktop open as AC10 expects. Loss is limited to settings written in that window; workaround is re-running after quitting Desktop, which the closing message already advises.
findings.recommendation: Compare the file mtime before the rename and return write-failed on a mismatch, or note the window beside the quit-first advice.

findings.title: BOM-prefixed config.json reported as invalid JSON
findings.problem: readFile(..., 'utf-8') keeps a leading U+FEFF and JSON.parse rejects it, so a BOM-prefixed config.json (for example saved by Windows PowerShell 5) returns outcome invalid-json (desktop-mcp-auth.ts:56-63).
findings.impact: Narrow trigger: a hand-edited, BOM-prefixed file on Windows; a file Desktop itself wrote has no BOM. It fails safe (file untouched, exit 1) but the user gets a misleading 'is not valid JSON' message and cannot reset until the BOM is removed.
findings.recommendation: Strip a leading U+FEFF from the text before calling parseJson.

findings.title: Server names printed with C1 controls and bidi unescaped
findings.problem: The header and formatServerNames claim a name cannot rewrite the lines after it, but JSON.stringify escapes only C0 controls, not C1 (U+0080-U+009F, including U+009B CSI) or bidi overrides (U+202E). Names have no length cap, only the count is capped at 20, and `path` is printed raw.
findings.impact: Narrow trigger: a server-name key holding C1 or bidi characters, or megabytes of text, which needs control over the MCP server list or config.json. Effect is spoofed or flooded terminal output only; no token or file excerpt is disclosed.
findings.recommendation: Replace C1 (U+007F-U+009F) and bidi (U+200E, U+200F, U+202A-U+202E, U+2066-U+2069) characters in each stringified name and truncate each name to about 80 characters, or soften the header comment.

findings.title: Result printing sits inside the platform-failure catch
findings.problem: reportResult runs inside the same try as getClaudeDesktopBaseDir and clearDesktopMcpSignIns, and reportUnexpectedFailure always prints 'Could not reset ... on platform <platform>' whatever was thrown, logging only the error code. A throw while printing or logging after the file was rewritten would report a platform failure with exit 1 though the sign-ins were cleared.
findings.impact: Reachability unconfirmed: no throw path was found in reportResult, but logger and sanitizeLogArgs internals were not traced. Today only the unsupported-platform throw reaches the catch, where the text is accurate, so this is a latent mis-report.
findings.recommendation: Keep getClaudeDesktopBaseDir and clearDesktopMcpSignIns in the try and call reportResult outside it, or word the catch text without naming the platform and log the error name.
